name: Wrench-Pyralis
description: Wrench-Pyralis is a volcanic world where tectonic forces have wrenched the crust into a chaotic jumble of overlapping plates, each one grinding against its neighbors in a continuous cycle of seismic violence. The planet's surface is a labyrinth of rift valleys and volcanic ridges, the landscape reshaping itself on timescales visible to the human eye as new eruptions build and destroy terrain in real time. Lava rivers pour through the rift valleys like veins of molten metal, their glow painting the toxic atmosphere in permanent shades of deep red and orange.

The heat and toxicity of Wrench-Pyralis are matched by its sheer geological instability. The ground shifts and buckles without warning, opening new fissures and closing existing ones in a tectonic rhythm that makes surface operations a gamble. Radiation hotspots mark locations where the crust is thinnest and the mantle's emissions are least attenuated, creating zones that would kill an unprotected human in minutes. The sky is a roiling mass of volcanic ash and sulfurous clouds that rain corrosive droplets and block all starlight.

A warship from the Border Conflicts lies broken across a rift valley, its hull twisted by a forced atmospheric entry that ended in catastrophe. The ship went down with its full complement and classified cargo, and the volatile surface has made recovery impossible. The wreck has sunk meters deeper into the terrain with each passing decade as lava flows slowly engulf it, and current projections suggest it will be completely buried within fifty years.

The classified cargo aboard the warship has kept Wrench-Pyralis on military watch lists for decades, with periodic reconnaissance flights confirming the wreck's position and progressive burial. Whatever the ship carried, it was important enough that the military would prefer it buried forever rather than risk it falling into unauthorized hands. The planet's own geology is cooperating, slowly entombing the warship in a coffin of basalt that will keep its secrets for geological ages.
